decisive_items: a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage surrounding the right kidney extending into the pelvis
hemoglobin of 6.5 g/dL and hematocrit of 28%, down from a baseline hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL and hematocrit of 38% one month prior
heterogeneous echogenicity around the right renal parenchyma
response.rationale: Acute flank pain with retroperitoneal hemorrhage, falling hemoglobin, and perirenal hematoma on imaging point to spontaneous renal hemorrhage; retroperitoneal hemorrhage is a descriptive finding, not the underlying renal source.

rejected.why: Imaging shows hemorrhage, not infarction; no ischemic evidence.
Describes the bleed location but lacks renal-specific etiology.
No infarction pattern; hemorrhage is primary, not secondary to infarction.
No aneurysm identified; renovascular source is speculative.
No prior procedure or fistula/pseudoaneurysm evidence.
